qaReadiness.summary: Repo has some Synthetic QA building blocks, but CodeVetter should ask for the missing runner/script/spec pieces before claiming runtime coverage.

readmePreview: A utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom user interfaces.

overview.summary: This is the Tailwind CSS v4 monorepo: a CSS-first utility framework whose compiler is a TypeScript AST pipeline (`packages/tailwindcss`) paired with a Rust candidate scanner compiled to a NAPI/WASM native addon (`crates/oxide` → `@tailwindcss/oxide`). Configuration moved out of `tailwind.config.js` and into CSS at-rules — `@theme`, `@utility`, `@custom-variant`, `@source`, `@plugin`, `@config`, `@apply` — with a dedicated `compat/` layer that replays legacy v3 JS configs and plugins onto the new design system. It ships as a fan of thin integration packages (CLI, PostCSS, Vite, webpack, Turbopack, browser CDN build, Bun-compiled standalone binary) that all wrap the same `compile()` + `Scanner` pair, plus an AST-driven `@tailwindcss/upgrade` codemod tool for v3→v4 migration. It targets web developers and build-tool authors; what's distinctive is the split-language architecture and the aggressive incremental-rebuild caching that appears in every integration.

system_map.summary: The repo is a pnpm workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`) orchestrated by Turborepo (`turbo.json`) layered over a Cargo workspace (`Cargo.toml`, `members = ["crates/*"]`). The compiler core lives in `packages/tailwindcss` and is pure TypeScript with no filesystem access — all IO is injected via `loadModule`/`loadStylesheet` callbacks. `@tailwindcss/node` is the Node IO adapter (enhanced-resolve + jiti + Lightning CSS), and `@tailwindcss/oxide` is the Rust scanner bridged through napi-rs. Six consumer packages (cli, postcss, vite, webpack, turbopack, browser, standalone) sit on top, and `@tailwindcss/upgrade` is a separate codemod CLI. There is no server or database; the storage layer is the filesystem plus in-memory LRU caches.

claims.claim: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` exports the three public compiler entrypoints — `compile(css, opts)` (string→string), `compileAst(ast, opts)` (AST→AST, used by the PostCSS plugin), and `__unstable__loadDesignSystem` (used by IntelliSense and the upgrade tool) — plus a default export that throws a hard error if someone wires `tailwindcss` directly into PostCSS.

The core compiler takes zero filesystem dependencies: `CompileOptions` declares `loadModule` and `loadStylesheet` callbacks that default to `throwOnLoadModule`/`throwOnLoadStylesheet`, which is what makes the same code run in Node, Bun, and the browser CDN build.

`@tailwindcss/node` is the Node runtime boundary: it wires `enhanced-resolve` resolvers (separate `cssResolver` with `mainFields: ['style']`, `esmResolver`, and `cjsResolver` fallback), `jiti` for `.ts` plugin/config files, and `Module.registerHooks({ resolve: resolveSync })` so ESM config reloads work in watch mode.

`crates/node/src/lib.rs` is the napi-rs bridge exposing the `Scanner` class (`scan()`, `scanFiles()`, `getCandidatesWithPositions()`, and `files`/`scannedFiles`/`globs`/`normalizedSources` getters) plus the `ChangedContent`, `GlobEntry`, and `SourceEntry` object shapes consumed by every JS integration.

The Cargo workspace has four crates: `tailwindcss-oxide` (the scanner/extractor), `tailwind-oxide` (`crates/node`, the NAPI shim), `classification-macros` (a `ClassifyBytes` proc-macro deriving byte-class lookup tables for the extractor state machines), and a vendored fork of BurntSushi's `ignore` crate pinned to edition 2024.

Build is `pnpm build` → `turbo build --filter=!./playgrounds/*`, followed by a `postbuild` hook that runs `scripts/pack-packages.mjs` to `pnpm pack` every non-private workspace into `dist/*.tgz` — the integration tests then install those tarballs.

Test commands are split three ways: `pnpm test` runs `cargo test && vitest run`, `pnpm test:integrations` runs `vitest --root=./integrations`, and `pnpm test:ui` runs Playwright in both `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/browser`.

`turbo.json` gives `@tailwindcss/oxide#build` explicit `inputs` covering `../oxide/src/**/*` and `../Cargo.toml`, so touching Rust source correctly busts the Turbo cache for the native addon; it also passes `RUSTUP_HOME` through via `globalPassThroughEnv`.

Deployment shape is npm publishing with provenance: `@tailwindcss/oxide` fans out into 12 platform-specific optionalDependencies (`napi.targets` includes `wasm32-wasip1-threads`), and `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds each target in a matrix then publishes with `id-token: write` for npm trusted publishing.

`@tailwindcss/standalone` is built by Bun (`bun ./scripts/build.ts`) into seven single-file executables (linux/macos/windows × arm64/x64, glibc and musl), each SHA-256 checksummed; it is marked `private: true` so `pack-packages.mjs` skips it.

Lightning CSS is the only output post-processor: `optimize()` in `@tailwindcss/node` runs `transform()` twice (so nesting-flattened adjacent rules get merged), pins browser targets to Safari/iOS 16.4, Firefox 128, Chrome 111, and uses `errorRecovery: true` with a warning filter for framework pseudo-classes like `::ng-deep` and `::v-deep`.
pnpm patches three dependencies — `@napi-rs/cli`, `@parcel/watcher`, and `lightningcss` — specifically so Bun can statically analyze them when compiling the standalone binary.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is (a) the CSS authoring language — a set of at-rules parsed in `parseCss`, (b) the `tailwindcss` CLI with `build` and `canonicalize` subcommands, (c) five build-tool integrations, (d) a zero-build browser CDN script, and (e) the `@tailwindcss/upgrade` migration CLI. The compat layer additionally re-exposes the entire v3 JS plugin API (`addUtilities`, `matchVariant`, `theme()`, etc.) so existing plugins keep working. IntelliSense-facing APIs (`getClassList`, `getVariants`, `canonicalizeCandidates`) are first-class exports of the design system rather than an afterthought.

claims.claim: The CSS at-rule vocabulary handled in `parseCss` is `@tailwind utilities`, `@utility`, `@source` (with `not`, `inline(…)`, and brace-expansion via `expand()`), `@variant`, `@custom-variant`, `@theme` (with `reference`/`inline`/`default`/`static`/`prefix(…)` options), `@apply`, `@import`, `@plugin`, and `@config`.

`@import "tailwindcss" theme(reference)`, `prefix(ident)`, `important`, and `source(…)` are implemented by rewriting the `@media` node that `postcss-import`-style resolution produces — `@media theme(reference)` is transformed into a `context({ reference: true })` wrapper rather than being a distinct parser path.
The `tailwindcss` CLI exposes `build` (default when no subcommand is given) and `canonicalize`, with root-level `--help` dispatch in `run()` that also errors on unknown non-flag commands.

`tailwindcss build` supports `--input/-i` (including `-` for stdin), `--output/-o`, `--watch[=always]`, `--poll[=ms]`, `--minify/-m`, `--optimize`, `--cwd`, `--map`, and `--silent`; when no `--input` is given it defaults to compiling `@import 'tailwindcss';`.

`tailwindcss canonicalize` rewrites candidate lists to their canonical form, reading from argv or stdin, with `--css` to point at a design-system entry, `--format text|json|jsonl`, and `--stream` for line-by-line stdin processing — aimed at tooling like Prettier plugins and linters.

`@tailwindcss/vite` ships as an array of three Vite plugins — `@tailwindcss/vite:scan` (config capture), `:generate:serve` (dev), and `:generate:build` (production, which additionally runs `optimize()`) — each with `transform.filter` id include/exclude regexes that skip `?raw`, `?url`, `?worker`, and CommonJS proxy requests.

`@tailwindcss/postcss` accepts `base`, `optimize` (defaults to `NODE_ENV === 'production'`), and `transformAssetUrls`, and bundles a `fixRelativePathsPlugin()` that repairs paths when `postcss-import` ran before it.

`@tailwindcss/webpack` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack` are near-identical webpack `LoaderContext` loaders taking `{ base, optimize }`, both keyed into a shared `QuickLRU` cache of max size 50 via `getCacheKey(resourceId, opts)`.

`@tailwindcss/browser` is a CDN build that reads `<style type="text/tailwindcss">` blocks, auto-injects `@import "tailwindcss";` when the user's CSS has no `@import`, and serves `tailwindcss`, `/preflight`, `/theme`, and `/utilities` from inlined `assets.css.*` strings; plugins and config files throw.

The v3 JS plugin API is fully re-implemented in `compat/plugin-api.ts`: `addBase`, `addVariant`, `matchVariant`, `addUtilities`, `matchUtilities`, `addComponents`/`matchComponents` (which just delegate to the utility variants), and a `theme()` function built by `createThemeFn`.

`tailwindcss` re-exports v3 compatibility entry points as separate package exports: `tailwindcss/colors`, `tailwindcss/defaultTheme`, `tailwindcss/plugin`, and `tailwindcss/lib/util/flattenColorPalette`, each with paired `.ts`/`.cts` implementations for ESM and CJS.

`@tailwindcss/upgrade` is a standalone migration CLI (`--config`, `--force`, `--version`) that refuses to run on a dirty git tree, migrates stylesheets, migrates `tailwind.config.js` into CSS, rewrites class names in templates, and then shells out to the detected package manager to bump `tailwindcss` and friends to `@latest`.

data_flow.summary: There are two independent input streams that converge at `build()`. Stream one is CSS: a stylesheet string is parsed by `CSS.parse`, `@import`s are inlined, at-rules are walked to populate a `Theme`, a `Utilities` registry, and a `Variants` registry, and the result is a `DesignSystem`. Stream two is candidates: the Rust `Scanner` walks the filesystem (gitignore-aware), pre-processes files by extension, runs byte-level state machines to extract class-name-shaped strings, and returns a sorted `Vec<String>` across the NAPI boundary. `build(candidates)` compiles those strings against the design system into AST nodes, splices them into the `@tailwind utilities` placeholder node, runs `optimizeAst`, and prints CSS via `toCss`. State ownership is explicit: `Theme` owns variables, `DesignSystem` owns caches, and the Rust `Scanner` owns file/mtime/candidate sets.

claims.claim: Input boundary one: `compile(css, opts)` calls `CSS.parse(css, { from })` then `parseCss`, which first wraps the AST in `contextNode({ base }, ast)` and resolves `@import`s through `substituteAtImports` before any at-rule walking happens.

`@theme` declarations are drained into a `Theme` map keyed by unescaped custom-property name, carrying `ThemeOptions` bit flags (`INLINE`, `REFERENCE`, `DEFAULT`, `STATIC`, `USED`) and a source location; `@keyframes` inside `@theme` are pulled out into `theme.addKeyframes` and re-hoisted as `atRoot` nodes.
The first `@theme` rule is replaced by a `:root, :host` style rule whose body is filled in *after* the compat hooks run, so JS-config theme extensions land in the same emitted variable block.

`@source` at-rules are split at parse time: `inline(...)` forms are brace-expanded into `inlineCandidates` (or `ignoredCandidates` when negated, which seed `designSystem.invalidCandidates`), while path forms become `{ base, pattern, negated }` entries returned as `compiler.sources`.

Every integration builds the scanner source list with the same three-branch rule: `root === 'none'` → no sources, `root === null` → `{ base, pattern: '**/*' }`, else the explicit `source(…)` root, concatenated with `compiler.sources`.

Input boundary two: `Scanner::scan()` calls `discover_sources()` (a `WalkBuilder` walk that populates `files`, `dirs`, `extensions`, and `mtimes`), then `extract_candidates()`, and returns a `par_sort_unstable`-sorted candidate vector.

File bytes are transformed before extraction: `pre_process_input(content, extension)` rewrites dialect-specific syntax (e.g. Pug/Haml/Slim shorthand) into something the generic extractor can read, then `Extractor::extract` runs a `CssVariableMachine` and a `CandidateMachine` over the bytes, emitting `Extracted::Candidate` and `Extracted::CssVariable`.

CSS files found during the walk are routed separately: `extract_candidates` calls `extract_css_variables` on them so that `--my-var` references in stylesheets count as used variables, distinct from utility candidates.

Candidate strings beginning with `--` are not compiled as utilities at all — `build()` routes them to `designSystem.theme.markUsedVariable(candidate)`, which is how theme variables referenced only from markup survive tree-shaking.

`compileCandidates` parses each raw candidate into `Candidate[]`, compiles each to AST nodes via `designSystem.compileAstNodes`, and sorts the result by a BigInt variant bitmask first, then by `GLOBAL_PROPERTY_ORDER` index, then by property count, then alphabetically — this is what produces Tailwind's stable output ordering.

Output boundary: `build()` mutates `utilitiesNode.nodes` in place, runs `optimizeAst(ast, designSystem, opts.polyfills)`, and `compile()`'s wrapper only re-runs `toCss` when the returned AST object identity changed — an explicit identity-based memoization.

Polyfills are a caller-controlled bitfield (`Polyfills.AtProperty`, `Polyfills.ColorMix`, `Polyfills.All`); the PostCSS plugin masks out `AtProperty` for `.module.css` files because the emitted global `*` rules break CSS Modules purity checks.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows matter most: a cold CLI build, a CLI watch-mode rebuild, and the Vite dev-server transform. All three share the same skeleton — create compiler, derive sources, construct `Scanner`, scan, build, write — but differ in how they decide between a full and an incremental rebuild. The browser CDN build is a fourth, MutationObserver-driven variant of the same loop. The distinguishing detail across all of them is that 'full rebuild' means *discarding and recreating the compiler*, while 'incremental' means only feeding new candidate strings into the existing one.

claims.claim: Cold CLI build order: `run()` → `build.handle(flags)` → resolve `--cwd`/`--input`/`--output` to absolute paths and reject identical in/out → read input (or `drainStdin()`, or default `@import 'tailwindcss';`) → `createCompiler(input, I)` → `scanner.scan()` → `compiler.build(candidates)` → `write(output, map, args, I)` → print `Done in …`.

`createCompiler` registers an `onDependency(path)` callback that pushes into `fullRebuildPaths`, and then deliberately appends a *negated* source for `path.basename(process.execPath)` so the standalone binary never scans itself — a rename-proof self-exclusion.
Watch mode calls `loadWatcher()` first (so a missing `@parcel/watcher` fails with a useful message before any watcher is registered), then `createWatchers(await watchDirectories(scanner), handle)`.

The watch handler short-circuits when the only changed file is `args['--output']`, preventing the write-triggers-rebuild infinite loop, then calls `getRebuildStrategy(files, fullRebuildPaths)` to choose a branch.

On a `full` rebuild the CLI does, in order: re-read input → `clearRequireCache(resolvedFullRebuildPaths)` → snapshot `backupRebuildPaths` → reset `fullRebuildPaths` → `createCompiler` → `scanner.scan()` → set up new watchers → tear down old watchers → `compiler.build(candidates)`.

On an `incremental` rebuild it calls `scanner.scanFiles(rebuildStrategy.changedFiles)` and returns early without writing if zero new candidates were found — so touching a file with no new classes costs no disk write.

The watch `catch` block restores `fullRebuildPaths = backupRebuildPaths` before logging, with an inline comment explaining the recovery case: deleting a transitive dependency of `tailwind.config.js` would otherwise leave the compiler permanently unable to re-register that dependency.

Polling mode is a separate code path from event-based watching: `--poll` is validated to be a positive number (default 250ms), and it drives a `fullRebuild(I)` closure plus cursor-hiding escape codes with `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers that exit 130/143.

Vite dev transform order: `isPotentialCssRootFile(id)` gate → look up a `Root` in `rootsByEnv` keyed by `this.environment?.name` → `root.generate(src, addWatchFile, I)` → return `{ code, map }`; returning `false` from `generate` deletes the root from the map so it can be garbage collected.

`Root.generate` decides to rebuild by calling `requiresBuild()`, which stats every entry in `buildDependencies` and returns true if any mtime advanced or any file is missing — an mtime-map strategy mirrored in the PostCSS and webpack plugins.

After compiling, `Root.generate` bails with `false` unless the compiler reported at least one of `Features.AtApply | JsPluginCompat | ThemeFunction | Utilities | Variants` — this is how ordinary non-Tailwind `.css` files pass through Vite untouched.

The PostCSS plugin has an even cheaper bail: before touching the cache it does a `root.walkAtRules` scan for any of `import|reference|theme|variant|config|plugin|apply|tailwind` and returns immediately if none are present.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is unusually thorough and layered: Vitest for ~80 co-located unit/snapshot suites, `cargo test` for the Rust scanner and the vendored `ignore` crate, a bespoke Vitest-based integration harness that materializes real temp projects and installs packed tarballs, and Playwright for browser-truth assertions about computed styles. CI runs unit and integration suites as two separate workflows, each with a three-OS matrix that is trimmed to Linux-only on feature branches unless the PR body contains `[ci-all]`. The gaps are mostly in the thin adapter layers — the CLI watch/poll machinery, the webpack/Turbopack loaders, and the release scripts have no direct unit tests.

claims.claim: Vitest is configured at the root with `projects: ['./packages/*']` and excludes `*.spec.*` files and `integrations/**` — the `.spec.ts` extension is reserved for Playwright so the two runners never collide.

Roughly 80 `*.test.ts` files live beside their sources under `packages/`, dominated by `utilities.test.ts` at ~31,600 lines and `index.test.ts` at ~7,300 lines — the utility matrix is tested exhaustively by snapshot.

`packages/tailwindcss/vitest.config.mts` registers a custom snapshot serializer at `src/test-utils/custom-serializer.ts`, which is why CSS snapshots read as formatted stylesheets rather than escaped strings.

Rust coverage centers on `crates/oxide/tests/scanner.rs` (~4,080 lines, 80+ `#[test]` cases inside a `mod scanner` block) covering source resolution, gitignore interaction, and symlink handling; the vendored `ignore` crate carries its own upstream tests.

The integration harness in `integrations/utils.ts` exports a custom `test(name, config, cb)` that mkdtemps a real project directory, writes a `fs` map of files, and hands the callback `exec`, `spawn`, `fs.expectFileToContain`, and `parseSourceMap` helpers.

Integration tests run against real packed tarballs: `PUBLIC_PACKAGES` is derived by reading `dist/` and mapping `tailwindcss-*.tgz` back to `@tailwindcss/*` names, which is why `pnpm build` must precede `pnpm test:integrations`.

There are 42 integration test files across six suites — `cli`, `oxide`, `postcss`, `turbopack`, `upgrade`, `vite`, `webpack` — with the Vite suite alone covering Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Qwik, React Router, Preact, Vue, CSS Modules, SSR, and source maps.

The integration harness compensates for known CI flakiness: timeouts are 120s on Windows vs 60s elsewhere, `retry` defaults to 2 under CI, and on Windows CI the temp root is derived from `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` because `tmpdir()` returns a `RUNNER~1` short path that breaks Vite builds.

Playwright covers browser-truth behavior that unit tests cannot: `packages/tailwindcss/tests/ui.spec.ts` (~2,480 lines) asserts *computed* values such as `touch-action` after `page.hover()` and resolved `linear-gradient(... in oklab ...)` strings.

The Playwright config sets Firefox `ui.primaryPointerCapabilities`/`ui.allPointerCapabilities` to `0x02 | 0x04` because headless Firefox otherwise reports no pointer, which would silently break every `hover:` variant assertion relying on `(hover: hover)`.

WebKit is skipped on Windows in both Playwright configs (a hanging-worker workaround) and the CI matrix pins macOS to `macos-15` for the unit job because Playwright 1.62+ dropped WebKit on macOS 14 and hangs rather than failing.

CI has two independent workflows: `ci.yml` (build → lint → `pnpm test` → Playwright) and `integration-tests.yml` (a 6-way `integration` matrix crossed with the OS matrix), both notifying Discord via `secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` on `main` failures.

risk_map.summary: Security surface is narrow but real: the compiler loads and executes arbitrary user JS via `@plugin`/`@config` through jiti, the upgrade CLI shells out to git and the package manager and rewrites source files in place, and the scanner walks the filesystem outside the repo root whenever `@source` points there. The larger operational risks are correctness-of-caching risks — every integration hand-rolls its own mtime-based invalidation, and the core `build()` explicitly assumes candidates are only ever added, never removed. Cross-platform fragility (Windows paths, symlinks, Bun/USERPROFILE) shows up repeatedly as inline workarounds, which is a reliable signal of where regressions land.

claims.claim: `@plugin` and `@config` execute arbitrary user code: `loadModule` resolves the id and calls `importModule`, which falls back to `createJiti(...).import(path)` when native `import()` fails — so a `.ts` config file is transpiled and run in-process with full Node privileges.

`globalThis.__tw_resolve` and `globalThis.__tw_load` are ambient global escape hatches consulted before every CSS and JS resolution; the standalone binary installs them to serve embedded assets, but any code loaded into the process can override module resolution by setting them.

`@tailwindcss/upgrade` shells out with `execSync` to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git status --porcelain`, and `npm ls tailwindcss --json`, then calls `pkgManager.add(...)` to install packages — it mutates the user's dependency tree as part of a 'migration'.

The upgrade tool's only safety net for in-place source rewriting is the `isRepoDirty()` check, which `--force` disables outright; after that it rewrites every matched CSS file and every template file via `writeFileSafely` with no backup.

Template rewriting is heuristic and acknowledged as such: `isSafeMigration` maintains hand-written regex denylists for Vue `v-if`, Alpine `wire:`, shadcn `variant:` props, Next.js `placeholder=`, and `$emit(` — any unlisted pattern risks a class-name rewrite inside a string that is not a class attribute.

File IO reaches outside the repo root by design: `SourceEntry::External` exists specifically to let `@source "../node_modules/my-lib"` bypass the default ignore rules, and `resolveJsId` extends module search with `process.env.NODE_PATH`.

`build()` carries a documented soundness assumption — 'this currently assumes that we only add new candidates and never remove any' — appearing twice as an early-return condition, so a candidate disappearing from source will not shrink the emitted CSS without a full rebuild.

Cache invalidation is duplicated four times with slightly different shapes: `Root.requiresBuild()` in Vite, the `context.mtimes` loop in PostCSS, `getRebuildStrategy` in the CLI, and per-loader `CacheEntry.mtimes` in webpack/Turbopack — a bug fixed in one will not propagate to the others.

`@tailwindcss/webpack` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack` are near-verbatim copies of each other down to identical `LoaderOptions`, `CacheEntry`, `getCacheKey`, and `getContextFromCache` definitions — divergence between them is a live duplication hazard.

The PostCSS plugin deliberately swallows errors — it `console.error`s and then throws `root.error(...)` after resetting `context.compiler = null`, with a comment that throwing directly 'will cause PostCSS to no longer watch for changes' — so genuine compile failures can surface as an empty stylesheet plus console noise.

The Vite plugin carries two hardcoded upstream-bug workarounds — skipping `addWatchFile` for the input file itself (Qwik) and ignoring `.svg` paths containing `#` or `?` (tailwindcss#16877) — meaning edits to those files silently do not trigger rebuilds.

Windows and symlink handling is a recurring fragility: the scanner canonicalizes via `dunce::canonicalize` with a cached parent-directory map, inserts both symlinked and canonical paths into `self.files`, and `scan_content` has to re-walk the tree to validate previously-unknown changed files.

extension_points.summary: The system has three distinct extension tiers. Tier one is CSS-native: `@utility`, `@custom-variant`, and `@theme` register directly into the design system with no JS. Tier two is the JS plugin API, preserved wholesale from v3 in `compat/plugin-api.ts` and loaded via `@plugin`. Tier three is internal: the `Utilities` and `Variants` classes are plain registries with `static`/`functional` methods that core code and plugins call identically, and the upgrade tool has its own ordered `DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS` array. Adding a new template language to the scanner is a matter of one new pre-processor module plus one match arm.

claims.claim: `Utilities` is the utility registry — `static(name, compileFn)` and `functional(name, compileFn, options)` push into a `DefaultMap<string, Utility[]>`, with a parallel `completions` map driving IntelliSense suggestions.

`Variants` is the variant registry, offering `static`, `functional`, and `fromAst(name, ast, designSystem)` (which powers `@custom-variant` with a body), and tracking `compounds`/`compoundsWith` bit flags that decide which variants may be composed with which.

`@utility` is the CSS-native extension point: `createCssUtility(node)` turns the at-rule into a `(designSystem) => void` registration function, with explicit validation that functional utilities end in `-*` and that `@utility` is never nested.

`@custom-variant` registrations are topologically sorted before application via `topologicalSort(customVariantDependencies, { onCircularDependency })`, so variants may reference each other and circular references produce a rendered CSS error rather than a stack overflow.

`buildPluginApi` is the JS plugin extension surface, exposing `addBase`, `addVariant`, `matchVariant`, `addUtilities`, `matchUtilities`, `addComponents`, `matchComponents`, and a `theme()` accessor, with name validation that rejects non-single-class selectors and non-lowercase-leading utility names.

`@plugin` supports typed options passed as a declaration body — `CssPluginOptions` values are parsed from the declaration text into JSON primitives (`null`, `true`, numbers, comma-separated lists) before being handed to the plugin factory.

`applyCompatibilityHooks` is the single seam where all v3 behavior is grafted on — it registers `darkModePlugin`, `registerContainerCompat`, `registerLegacyUtilities`, `registerScreensConfig`, and `registerThemeVariantOverrides`, keeping legacy concerns out of core.

`DesignSystem.storage` is an explicit general-purpose extension slot — a `Record<symbol, unknown>` documented as requiring unique symbol keys to avoid collisions; the canonicalization code uses it via `prepareDesignSystemStorage` and `UTILITY_SIGNATURE_KEY`.

Adding a new template language to the scanner requires two edits: a new module in `crates/oxide/src/extractor/pre_processors/` re-exported from `mod.rs`, and a new extension arm in the `pre_process_input` match statement.

The extractor is itself a pluggable set of state machines all implementing the `Machine` trait — `ArbitraryPropertyMachine`, `ArbitraryValueMachine`, `NamedUtilityMachine`, `NamedVariantMachine`, `ModifierMachine`, `StringMachine`, and others — which `main.rs` can benchmark individually via `_run_machine::<T>`.

The upgrade tool's template codemods are an ordered array `DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS: Migration[]` where each entry is `(designSystem, userConfig, rawCandidate) => string`; order is load-bearing, flagged by the inline comment that `migrateVariantOrder` must run before variant-modifying migrations.

CSS-level codemods are a parallel, separately-composed pipeline in `codemods/css/` (`migrate-at-apply`, `migrate-at-layer-utilities`, `migrate-import`, `migrate-media-screen`, `migrate-preflight`, `migrate-tailwind-directives`, `migrate-theme-to-var`, `migrate-variants-directive`), each with a co-located test file.

agent_handoff.summary: Read the core compiler before touching anything: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` (`parseCss` → `compileAst` → `compile`), then `design-system.ts` and `compile.ts`. Almost every behavioral change belongs in `packages/tailwindcss` or `crates/oxide`, not in the integration packages — those are thin and near-duplicative on purpose. Conventions are enforced mechanically: Prettier config lives inline in the root `package.json` (no semicolons, single quotes, 100 columns, organize-imports), and `pnpm lint` runs `prettier --check` plus `turbo lint` (which is `tsc --noEmit` per package). The project explicitly does not accept feature PRs without prior discussion, and does not accept any PR without tests.

claims.claim: Read first, in order: `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` (the at-rule walk and `build()` contract), `packages/tailwindcss/src/design-system.ts` (the `DesignSystem` type and its caches), `packages/tailwindcss/src/compile.ts` (candidate → AST + sorting), and `crates/oxide/src/scanner/mod.rs` (the scan lifecycle).

Setup is `pnpm install`, `rustup default stable`, `rustup target add wasm32-wasip1-threads`, then `pnpm build`; the WASM target is mandatory because `@tailwindcss/oxide`'s `build` script always runs `build:wasm` after `build:platform`.
Day-to-day loop is `pnpm tdd` (Vitest watch with `--hideSkippedTests`); for browser or integration behavior you must run `pnpm build` first because both harnesses consume built artifacts.
Before submitting: run `pnpm test` (cargo + vitest), `pnpm build && pnpm test:integrations`, `pnpm build && pnpm test:ui`, and `pnpm run lint`; `pnpm run format` auto-fixes style.

Code style is Prettier with `semi: false`, `singleQuote: true`, `printWidth: 100`, and `prettier-plugin-organize-imports`; `integrations/**/*.ts` additionally uses `prettier-plugin-embed` so embedded CSS/HTML template literals are formatted.

Safe edit boundary: the core compiler must stay IO-free. Anything needing `fs`, module resolution, or Lightning CSS belongs in `@tailwindcss/node`, which is the only package allowed to be the bridge between core and the runtime.

A change to utility or variant output almost always needs a snapshot update in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts` or `variants.test.ts`, plus a check of `packages/tailwindcss/src/__snapshots__/`; these files are enormous, so target specific test names rather than running the whole suite.

Trap: output ordering is not alphabetical. It is governed by `GLOBAL_PROPERTY_ORDER` in `property-order.ts` combined with a BigInt variant bitmask; reordering that array silently reshuffles every generated stylesheet.

Trap: `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test'` gates both the license banner comment prepended in `compileAst` and the Lightning CSS warning output, so CSS produced under test differs from production output.

Trap: the integration packages duplicate the same source-derivation block (`root === 'none'` / `root === null` / explicit root, concat `compiler.sources`). Changing that contract in core requires updating the CLI, Vite, PostCSS, webpack, and Turbopack call sites together.

Trap: Rust edits need `pnpm build` (or `pnpm --filter @tailwindcss/oxide build`) to regenerate the `.node` addon before JS tests see them; `turbo.json` declares the cross-crate `inputs` that make this cache correctly.

Debugging hook: set `DEBUG=1` (or `DEBUG=tailwindcss`) to enable the `Instrumentation` timers that bracket every phase — 'Setup compiler', 'Scan for candidates', 'Build CSS', 'Optimize CSS' — across the CLI, Vite, PostCSS, and loaders.

readmePreview: Vite ⚡ Next Generation Frontend Tooling - 💡 Instant Server Start - ⚡️ Lightning Fast HMR - 🛠️ Rich Features - 📦 Optimized Build - 🔩 Universal Plugin Interface - 🔑 Fully Typed APIs Vite (French word for "quick", pronounced /viːt/, like "veet") is a build t

overview.summary: This is the Vite monorepo (`@vitejs/vite-monorepo`) at v8.3.0 — a pnpm workspace shipping three published packages: `vite` (the native-ESM dev server + Rolldown-powered bundler), `create-vite` (the scaffolding CLI), and `@vitejs/plugin-legacy` (SystemJS/Babel downlevel output for old browsers). The `vite` package is the bulk of it: a `cac`-driven CLI over four commands (dev/build/optimize/preview), a `connect` middleware stack that transforms modules on demand and pushes HMR over an authenticated WebSocket, and a Rollup-compatible plugin container that now runs on Rolldown/Oxc rather than Rollup+esbuild. What's distinctive at this commit is the Environment API — dev and build are both fanned out across named environments (`client`, `ssr`, custom) each with its own module graph, plugin container and optimizer — plus an experimental `bundledDev` mode that swaps the per-module transform pipeline for a lazy Rolldown dev bundle served from memory. Correctness is enforced almost entirely by a 83-playground / 109-spec Playwright+Vitest integration suite that runs every fixture in serve, bundled-dev, and build modes.

system_map.summary: Three publishable packages under `packages/`, a 83-directory `playground/` that doubles as the integration test corpus, and a VitePress `docs/` site deployed to Netlify. The `vite` package's runtime splits four ways: `src/node` (server, build, config, plugins — Node only), `src/client` (browser HMR client and error overlay), `src/module-runner` (SSR/runtime module evaluation), and `src/shared` (code compiled into both sides). All bundling — of Vite itself, of user configs, of dep pre-bundles, and of production output — goes through Rolldown; Rollup remains only as a type source and devDependency. There is no database or persistent store; the only on-disk state is the dep-optimizer cache under `cacheDir` and build output under `outDir`.

claims.claim: The published CLI entry is `packages/vite/bin/vite.js`, a thin launcher that enables source maps, installs an `unhandledRejection` trap, parses `-d/--debug`, `-f/--filter` and `--profile` out of `process.argv` *before* importing `../dist/node/cli.js`, and calls `module.enableCompileCache()` with a 10s `flushCompileCache` timer.

`packages/vite/src/node/cli.ts` registers exactly four `cac` commands: the default `[root]` (aliased `serve` and `dev`), `build [root]`, `optimize [root]` (marked deprecated in its own description), and `preview [root]`; each dynamically `import()`s its implementation module so the dev path never loads `build.ts`.

The package's public API surface is `packages/vite/src/node/index.ts`, which re-exports `createServer`, `build`, `createBuilder`, `preview`, `optimizeDeps`, `defineConfig`/`resolveConfig`/`loadConfigFromFile`, `runnerImport`, `fetchModule`, `createServerHotChannel`, `transformWithOxc`, `preprocessCSS`, and `parseAst`/`parseAstAsync` aliased from Rolldown.

`package.json` `exports` publishes four entry points — `.` → `dist/node/index.js`, `./module-runner` → `dist/node/module-runner.js`, `./internal` → `dist/node/internal.js`, and raw `./dist/client/*` — with `./types/internal/*` explicitly nulled to keep internal types unreachable.

Vite builds itself with Rolldown, not Rollup: `rolldown.config.ts` emits separate browser bundles for `src/client/env.ts` → `dist/client/env.mjs`, `src/client/clientEntry.ts` → `dist/client/client.mjs`, and `src/client/bundledDevClient.ts` → `dist/client/bundledDevClient.mjs`, plus a Node ESM bundle with `node/[name].js` entries and `node/chunks/` shared chunks.

The dev server is a `connect()` app, not a framework: `_createServer` builds `middlewares = connect()`, wraps it in `resolveHttpServer`, attaches `createWebSocketServer`, and creates a `chokidar` watcher over root + `config.configFileDependencies` + env files + `publicDir`.

Runtime state is owned per-environment, not globally: `_createServer` iterates `config.environments` calling `environmentOptions.dev.createEnvironment(name, config, { ws })` and `environment.init({ watcher, previousInstance })`, so each of `client`/`ssr`/custom gets its own `DevEnvironment` with its own `moduleGraph` and `pluginContainer`.

The legacy flat `server.moduleGraph` / `server.pluginContainer` / `server.transformRequest` APIs still exist but are getters that call `warnFutureDeprecation(config, 'removeServerModuleGraph')` etc. and delegate to the client environment via a `ModuleGraph` facade in `mixedModuleGraph.ts`.

Production builds go through `createBuilder` → `builder.buildApp()` → per-environment `buildEnvironment()`, which calls `resolveRolldownOptions(environment, chunkMetadataMap)` then `rolldown(...)` and `bundle.write|generate`; `--watch` instead returns a Rolldown `watch()` watcher wired to BUNDLE_START/BUNDLE_END/ERROR events.

The pnpm workspace spans `packages/*`, `playground/**`, nested `packages/**/__tests__/**`, and `docs`, with `overrides: { vite: 'workspace:*' }` so every playground resolves the local build, and patched deps for `sirv@3.0.2`, `chokidar@3.6.0` and `dotenv-expand@13.0.0`.

Build/test commands are all at the root: `pnpm build` (`pnpm -r --filter='./packages/*' run build`), `pnpm test` = `test-unit && test-serve && test-build`, plus `test-serve-bundled` which sets `VITE_TEST_BUNDLED_DEV=1`, and `ci-publish` (`tsx scripts/publishCI.ts`).

Docs are a separate VitePress app (`@vitejs/monorepo-docs`) with a 592-line `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`, deployed by Netlify via `command = "pnpm ci-docs"` publishing `docs/.vitepress/dist`, gated by `scripts/docs-check.sh` as the ignore predicate.

feature_catalog.summary: Vite's user-facing surface is four CLI commands, a programmatic JS API, a Rollup-superset plugin hook system, and a browser-side HMR runtime with an error overlay. Around that sit optional subsystems: dependency pre-bundling, CSS preprocessing and modules, worker/WASM/asset handling, `import.meta.glob`, SSR module running, and the legacy-browser plugin. `create-vite` is an independent interactive scaffolder with eleven framework families. The most recently added features are the multi-environment builder (`--app` / `builder: {}`), console forwarding from browser to terminal, and `--experimentalBundle` bundled dev.

claims.claim: `vite dev` accepts `--host`, `--port`, `--open [path]`, `--cors`, `--strictPort`, `--force` (bust the optimizer cache) and `--experimentalBundle`, then prints URLs and installs CLI shortcuts, adding a `p` shortcut to toggle the CPU profiler when launched under `--profile`.

`vite build` exposes `--target`, `--outDir`, `--assetsDir`, `--assetsInlineLimit`, `--ssr [entry]`, `--sourcemap [inline|hidden]`, `--minify [oxc|terser|esbuild]` (default `oxc`), `--manifest`, `--ssrManifest`, `--emptyOutDir`, `-w/--watch`, and `--app` which is sugar for `builder: {}`.
Interactive terminal shortcuts during dev are `r` restart server, `u` show server url, `o` open in browser, `c` clear console, `q` quit; preview mode registers only `o` and `q`.

The dev server exposes built-in HTTP endpoints beyond module serving: `/__open-in-editor` (via `launch-editor-middleware`), a `viteHMRPingMiddleware` answering `accept: text/x-vite-ping` with 204, and `/@fs/` raw filesystem serving guarded by the allow-list.

A dev proxy is available via `server.proxy`, backed by `http-proxy-3`, supporting `rewrite`, `configure`, webpack-dev-server-style `bypass`, WebSocket proxying, and `rewriteWsOrigin` to rewrite the Origin header on WS upgrades.

The browser client ships an error overlay implemented as the custom element `vite-error-overlay` (`class ErrorOverlay extends HTMLElement`), gated by the injected `__HMR_ENABLE_OVERLAY__` define and creatable/clearable from `handleMessage`.

Dependency pre-bundling is a full subsystem: `scanImports` computes entries and runs a Rolldown scanner, `runOptimizeDeps` writes a `_metadata.json` cache under `getDepsCacheDir(environment)`, and `loadCachedDepOptimizationMetadata` / `cleanupDepsCacheStaleDirs` manage reuse and GC across runs.

The built-in plugin pipeline provides asset handling, CSS (`cssPlugin`/`cssPostPlugin`/`cssAnalysisPlugin`), HTML (`htmlInlineProxyPlugin`/`buildHtmlPlugin`), web workers (`webWorkerPlugin`, `workerImportMetaUrlPlugin`), WASM (`wasmHelperPlugin`), `define`, `import.meta.glob` (`importGlobPlugin`), dynamic-import variables, and module-preload polyfill.

Browser console forwarding to the terminal is opt-in via `server.forwardConsole.enabled`, which conditionally inserts `forwardConsolePlugin({ environments: ['client'] })` into the pipeline and is picked up client-side through the `__SERVER_FORWARD_CONSOLE__` define.

SSR is served by `fetchModule(environment, url, importer)`, which short-circuits `data:` URLs and Node builtins to `{externalize, type:'builtin'}`, external URLs to `type:'network'`, and otherwise resolves bare specifiers through `tryNodeResolve` with `externalConditions`.

`vite/module-runner` is a separately published runtime: `class ModuleRunner` with `evaluatedModules`, a pluggable `transport` that `invoke('fetchModule', ...)`s the server, optional HMR via `createHMRHandlerForRunner`, and `cachedRequest`/`directRequest` for circular-dependency-aware evaluation.

`create-vite` v9.2.1 is an interactive prompt-driven scaffolder over a `FRAMEWORKS` table covering vanilla, vue, react, preact, lit, svelte, solid and qwik, each with TS/JS variants plus links to external starters (Nuxt, Vike, Official Vue Starter), materialised from the sibling `template-*` directories.

data_flow.summary: Three input boundaries feed the system: the config file (loaded by bundling, runner-import, or native import), `.env` files filtered by prefix, and HTTP/WS requests from the browser. Config flows into a single frozen `ResolvedConfig` that fans out into per-environment configs; each `DevEnvironment` then owns a `EnvironmentModuleGraph` as the authoritative in-memory state. A request's data path is URL → plugin container `resolveId`→`load`→`transform` → optional `ssrTransform` → cached `TransformResult` (code + map + etag + deps) stored on the module node and written back out through `send()`. The reverse direction — file change → HMR payload → WebSocket → browser — is the only push channel. In build mode the same plugin container is driven by Rolldown instead of by HTTP requests, and the terminal output boundary is `outDir` plus optional `manifest.json`/`ssr-manifest.json`.

claims.claim: Config entry: `resolveConfig` merges inline config over the file config from `loadConfigFromFile`, then re-derives `mode`, filters plugins by `apply`, runs `config` hooks via `runConfigHook`, and force-injects `client` (and usually `ssr`) into `config.environments` before per-environment resolution.

`loadConfigFromFile` picks one of three loaders selected by `--configLoader`: `bundleAndLoadConfigFile` (default — Rolldown-bundles the config then evaluates it), `runnerImportConfigFile` (uses Vite's own module runner), or `nativeImportConfigFile` (raw `import()` of a `file://` URL with a `?t=` cache-buster, or `fresh-import`).

Env vars enter through `loadEnv(mode, envDir, prefixes = 'VITE_')`, which reads `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.<mode>`, `.env.<mode>.local` (accepting FIFOs so 1Password-style pipes work), parses with `node:util` `parseEnv`, then expands with `dotenv-expand` against a *copy* of `process.env` so expansion doesn't mutate the global.

`transformRequest(environment, url, options)` dedupes concurrent work through `environment._pendingRequests` keyed by timestamp-stripped URL, and records a `monotonicDateNow()` timestamp up front so a transform that races an invalidation is discarded rather than cached stale.

Inside `loadAndTransform` the order is `pluginContainer.load(id)` → fall back to reading from disk → `pluginContainer.transform(code, id, ...)` → `ssrTransform(code, normalizedMap, url, originalCode, ...)` when the environment needs module-runner output.

The transform result carries `{ code, map, ssr?, etag?, deps?, dynamicDeps? }`; the etag is what `cachedTransformMiddleware` matches against `if-none-match` via `moduleGraph.getModuleByEtag` to short-circuit with a 304.

`importAnalysisPlugin` is the rewrite stage that converts every import specifier to a server-resolvable URL via its internal `normalizeUrl`, records importer/imported edges on the module graph, and computes `isSelfAccepting` from `import.meta.hot.accept` calls — the data the HMR propagation algorithm later consumes.

HMR output is one of two payload shapes computed in `updateModules`: a `{type:'full-reload', triggeredBy, path}` message, or a `{type:'update', updates:[...]}` array whose entries carry `path`, `acceptedPath`, `explicitImportRequired`, `isWithinCircularImport` and `firstInvalidatedBy`.

Client-side the payload arrives over a `normalizeModuleRunnerTransport`-wrapped WebSocket opened to `${protocol}://${socketHost}?token=${wsToken}` with subprotocol `vite-hmr`, and is dispatched by `handleMessage` into `hmrClient.queueUpdate(update)`.

Static assets bypass the transform pipeline entirely: `servePublicMiddleware` is registered *before* `transformMiddleware` specifically so `publicDir` files are served as-is, and `serveRawFsMiddleware` handles `/@fs/`-prefixed absolute paths by slicing `FS_PREFIX` off the pathname.

In bundled-dev mode the data path inverts: Rolldown produces output files that `BundledDev` stores as lazily-evaluated entries in `MemoryFiles` (including `BUNDLED_DEV_CLIENT_FILENAME`), and `memoryFilesMiddleware` serves from that map instead of from the module graph.

Build-mode data flow is fanned out by environment: `createBuilder` re-runs `resolveConfigToBuild` once per environment name (unless `configBuilder.sharedConfigBuild`) with a `patchPlugins` pass that swaps in shared plugin instances for those marked `sharedDuringBuild`.

behavior_traces.summary: Four flows are worth tracing: dev-server startup, a module request, a file-change HMR round trip, and a production build. Startup is notable for deferring `buildStart` and optimizer init until the HTTP `listen` call is intercepted. The module request path is a long but linear middleware chain. HMR distinguishes config/env changes (full server restart) from module changes (graph propagation). The build path is a per-environment loop over Rolldown.

claims.claim: Dev startup: `bin/vite.js` → `dist/node/cli.js` → the default cac action → `createServer()` → `_createServer` → `disableCache()` → `resolveConfig(inlineConfig,'serve')` → `resolveHttpServer` → `createWebSocketServer` → chokidar watcher → per-environment `createEnvironment`/`init` → middleware registration → `server.listen()`.

Startup defers expensive work by monkey-patching the HTTP server: `httpServer.listen` is replaced with a wrapper that awaits `initServer(true)` first and re-emits any error as an `'error'` event, so `buildStart` and `environment.listen(server)` run exactly once before the socket binds.
In middleware mode there is no HTTP server at all — `httpServer` is `null`, `resolveHttpServer` is skipped, and `initServer(false)` is awaited inline at the end of `_createServer`.

The middleware chain is registered in a fixed order: `timeMiddleware` (only when `process.env.DEBUG`) → `rejectInvalidRequestMiddleware` → `corsMiddleware` → `hostValidationMiddleware` → user `configureServer` hooks → `cachedTransformMiddleware` → `proxyMiddleware` → `baseMiddleware` → `/__open-in-editor` → HMR ping → `servePublicMiddleware` → `transformMiddleware` → `serveRawFsMiddleware` → `serveStaticMiddleware` → `htmlFallbackMiddleware` → post hooks → `indexHtmlMiddleware` → `notFoundMiddleware` → `errorMiddleware`.

`configureServer` hooks run in two phases around the internal middlewares: the hook's synchronous body runs before `cachedTransformMiddleware` is added, while any function it *returns* is pushed to `postHooks` and invoked after the static/HTML-fallback middlewares but before `indexHtmlMiddleware`, which is what lets user middleware pre-empt `index.html`.

A module request runs `transformMiddleware` → `environment.transformRequest(url)` → `transformRequest` (pending-request dedupe) → `doTransform` (`pluginContainer.resolveId`) → `loadAndTransform` (`pluginContainer.load`, then `pluginContainer.transform`) → optional `ssrTransform` → `send()` with the etag.

`EnvironmentPluginContainer.resolveId` lazily triggers `this.buildStart()` and awaits `_buildStartPromise` on the first resolution, so for non-client environments the `buildStart` hook fires on first request rather than at server boot.

File change → `watcher.on('change')` → `onFileChange` → `handleHMRUpdate(type, file, server)`, which first checks whether the file is `config.configFile`, a member of `config.configFileDependencies`, or an env file for the current mode — any of those triggers `restartServerWithUrls(server)` instead of an HMR update.

`handleHMRUpdate` snapshots `server.environments` and defines `isStale()` comparing identity, because a `hotUpdate`/`handleHotUpdate` plugin hook may restart the server mid-transaction and invalidate the whole HMR pass.

Edits to Vite's own client directory can't be hot-updated: if the changed file starts with `normalizedClientDir`, every environment immediately gets `hot.send({ type:'full-reload', path:'*' })` and the function returns.

`updateModules` runs `propagateUpdate(mod, traversedModules, boundaries)` per changed module, invalidates via `moduleGraph.invalidateModule`, and escalates to full reload on any dead end, on an empty `modules` array, on `circular import invalidate`, or when a client-environment `.html` file changes and none of its modules are of type `js`.

Production build: `cli.ts` build action → `createBuilder(inlineConfig, null)` → `builder.buildApp()` → sorted `buildApp` plugin hooks with `configBuilder.buildApp(builder)` interleaved before `order:'post'` hooks → fallback loop calling `builder.build(environment)` for any environment still `!isBuilt` → `buildEnvironment` → `rolldown()` → `bundle.write()` → `builder.runDevTools()`.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is Vitest-only, split into two configs. `vitest.config.ts` collects 68 unit specs from `**/__tests__/**/*.spec.[tj]s` inside `packages/`, running with `isolate: false` and a 20s timeout. `vitest.config.e2e.ts` collects 109 integration specs from `playground/**`, driving a real Playwright Chromium browser against real Vite servers. The integration suite is the primary correctness net and runs three times in CI — serve, bundled-dev, and build — across Node 20/22/24/26 on Ubuntu plus macOS and Windows. The weakest spot is that unit coverage of the largest files is thin relative to their size: `css.ts` (3685 lines) and `hmr.ts` (1193 lines) have no dedicated unit spec, and are covered only indirectly through playground fixtures.

claims.claim: Unit tests use `vitest.config.ts` with `include: ['**/__tests__/**/*.spec.[tj]s']`, explicitly excluding `./playground/**` and `./playground-temp/**`, `testTimeout: 20000`, `isolate: false`, and an alias mapping `vite/module-runner` to the TypeScript source rather than `dist`.

There are 68 unit spec files under `packages/**/__tests__/`, concentrated in `packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/` (config, build, dev, env, html, http, resolve, scan, utils, oxc, packages, shortcuts, external, environment, filterRegex, assetSource) plus `plugins/`, `optimizer/` and `utils/` subdirectories.

Integration tests use `vitest.config.e2e.ts` with `include: ['./playground/**/*.spec.[tj]s']`, `globalSetup: playground/vitestGlobalSetup.ts`, `setupFiles: playground/vitestSetup.ts`, `reporters: 'dot'`, and a timeout of 50s on CI / 30s locally (Infinity under `PWDEBUG`).

`vitestGlobalSetup.ts` launches a shared `chromium.launchServer()` (headed when `VITE_DEBUG_SERVE` is set, `--no-sandbox` on CI), shares the endpoint via `project.provide('wsEndpoint', ...)`, then copies only the playground directories actually referenced by the selected test files into `playground-temp/`.

`vitestSetup.ts` exposes the per-test harness — `page`, `viteTestUrl`, `browserLogs`, `browserErrors`, `serverLogs`, and mode flags `isBuild`/`isServe`/`isBundledDev`/`isBundled` — aliased in tests as `~utils`.

The same 109 playground specs are executed under three different modes selected by env vars: default serve, `VITE_TEST_BUNDLED_DEV=1` (`test-serve-bundled`), and `VITE_TEST_BUILD=1` (`test-build`), with `NODE_ENV` set to `production` only in the build run.

Known gaps in bundled-dev mode are tracked as an explicit 22-entry `bundledDevExclude` array in `vitest.config.e2e.ts` — including `fs-serve`, `csp`, `hmr-ssr`, `optimize-deps`, `tailwind` and all four `worker` variants — with the convention that partial failures use `test.skipIf(isBundledDev)` instead of listing the file.

CI runs the full matrix Node 20/22/24/26 on ubuntu-latest plus macos-latest@24 and windows-latest@24.15.0 (pinned to work around nodejs/node#63638), with `fail-fast: false` and a 20-minute timeout per job.

The CI `test` job runs all four suites sequentially — `test-unit`, `test-serve`, `test-serve-bundled`, `test-build` — after a `pnpm run build`, and a separate `lint` job runs eslint, `pnpm format && git diff --exit-code`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test-docs`.

CI skips the whole test matrix when only docs, `.github/**` (excluding `ci.yml`), `packages/create-vite/template**`, or `**.md` changed, via a `changed` job using `tj-actions/changed-files` with `only_changed`.
Flakiness is managed with environment knobs rather than retries in test code: `VITEST_SEGFAULT_RETRY: 3` and `NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=6144` are set globally in the workflow env block.

A scheduled Semgrep scan (`--config auto`, weekly on Tuesdays) uploads SARIF to GitHub code scanning, but explicitly excludes `playground` and `__tests__` and disables the `detect-non-literal-regexp` rule — so dynamic regex construction in source is not flagged.

risk_map.summary: Vite's security model rests on four independent guards — the `server.fs` allow/deny list, WebSocket token authentication, host validation, and CORS origin restriction — and a bypass in any one of them exposes the developer's filesystem or dev server to a hostile web page. The code shows scar tissue from past CVEs: Windows 8.3 short-name detection, NTFS ADS colon rejection, `#`-in-URL rejection, and trailing-slash normalisation are all defensive patches with explanatory comments. Beyond security, the main structural risks are the very large monolithic modules (`css.ts` at 3685 lines, `config.ts` at 2961), the two-implementation split between classic dev and `bundledDev`, and a large surface of deprecated-but-live compatibility shims.

claims.claim: `isFileLoadingAllowed` is the single chokepoint for filesystem access and carries three separate bypass mitigations: Windows 8.3 short-name paths (`PROGRA~1`, matched by `windowsShortNameSegmentRE`) are rejected outright, any `:` outside a drive letter is rejected as a possible NTFS alternate data stream, and trailing slashes are stripped before the deny check because `fs.readFile('/foo.png/')` resolves to `/foo.png`.

`server.fs.deny` defaults to only six patterns — `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.{crt,pem,key,p12,pfx,cer,der}`, `.npmrc`, `.yarnrc.yml`, `**/.git/**` — so any other secret-bearing file inside an allowed root (e.g. `credentials.json`, `.aws/`, `id_rsa` without extension) is servable when `fs.strict` passes.

`config.safeModulePaths` is an escape hatch checked *before* the `fs.allow` list in `isFileLoadingAllowed`, and it is populated at runtime by `DevEnvironment._registerInputsAsSafeModules()` — meaning build inputs silently widen the serving allow-list.

`rejectInvalidRequestMiddleware` exists specifically because Node accepts `#` in request targets while the `server.fs.deny` checks assume it is absent — a 400 is returned for any URL containing `#`, and this middleware is the first in the chain.

WebSocket auth uses a per-process 72-bit token compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, but the token travels as a URL query parameter (`?token=...`), which the comment acknowledges may land in server/middleware logs.
`config.legacy.skipWebSocketTokenCheck` is a live opt-out that disables token validation entirely inside `shouldHandle`, re-opening cross-site WebSocket hijacking for anyone who sets it.

Host validation is skipped whenever `server.https` is configured (`if (allowedHosts !== true && !serverConfig.https)`), on the reasoning that HTTPS is not DNS-rebinding-vulnerable — so a misissued or self-signed HTTPS dev setup loses that guard.

The WS upgrade path allows *any* non-browser client without a token: `shouldHandle` returns `true` when `req.headers.origin` is absent, with an inline comment justifying it for backward compat — meaning any local process that can open a socket can join the HMR channel.

Shell-out surface exists in the dev server itself: `server/index.ts` imports `execSync` from `node:child_process`, and `openBrowser.ts` spawns a browser process honouring the `BROWSER`/`BROWSER_ARGS` environment variables which `loadEnv` will populate from a project's `.env` file.

Config loading executes arbitrary project code by design through three paths (`bundleAndLoadConfigFile`, `runnerImportConfigFile`, `nativeImportConfigFile`), and `bundleConfigFile`/`loadConfigFromBundledFile` evaluate the bundled result — so opening an untrusted repo and running `vite` is code execution.

Blast-radius hotspots by size: `plugins/css.ts` (3685 lines), `config.ts` (2961), `utils.ts` (2022), `build.ts` (1986), `plugins/html.ts` (1753), `server/index.ts` (1496), `server/pluginContainer.ts` (1332) — none of which has a same-named unit spec except `config.spec.ts`, `build.spec.ts` and `html.spec.ts`.

The dev server now has two divergent implementations gated on one boolean: `config.experimental.bundledDev` swaps the entire serving strategy, skips `cachedTransformMiddleware`, skips `buildStart` at init, and short-circuits `handleHMRUpdate` with a `// TODO: support handleHotUpdate / hotUpdate` early return — so plugin HMR hooks silently do nothing in that mode.

extension_points.summary: Vite's primary extension mechanism is the plugin object — a superset of Rolldown/Rollup's, adding `config`, `configEnvironment`, `configureServer`, `configurePreviewServer`, `transformIndexHtml`, `hotUpdate`, `buildApp`, and the environment-scoping fields `applyToEnvironment`/`sharedDuringBuild`. The ordered array returned by `resolvePlugins` is the canonical insertion-point table: user `pre`, `normal` and `post` plugins are spliced at three fixed positions between internal plugins. Beyond plugins, the extension surface includes the environment factory (`dev.createEnvironment`/`build.createEnvironment`), the hot-channel/transport abstraction, the CLI shortcut table, and the `create-vite` template directory convention.

claims.claim: `resolvePlugins(config, prePlugins, normalPlugins, postPlugins)` is the ordering contract: user `pre` plugins land after the alias plugins, `normal` plugins after asset/CSS/worker handling but before `definePlugin`, and `post` plugins after the glob/dynamic-import plugins — with `clientInjectionsPlugin`, `cssAnalysisPlugin` and `importAnalysisPlugin` always last.

`getSortedPluginsByHook(hookName, plugins)` implements the per-hook `order: 'pre' | 'post'` sorting with three running indices, and `createPluginHookUtils` memoises the result per hook name into `getSortedPlugins`/`getSortedPluginHooks` on the resolved config.

`applyToEnvironment(environment)` lets a plugin opt in/out per environment or return a *replacement* plugin — as the built-in alias plugin does, swapping itself for Rolldown's native `nativeAliasPlugin` when `environment.config.isBundled` and no custom resolver is present.
`perEnvironmentPlugin(name, applyToEnvironment)` is the public helper for building environment-scoped plugins, exported from the package root alongside `perEnvironmentState`.

`buildApp` is the multi-environment build orchestration hook: `builder.buildApp()` walks `config.getSortedPlugins('buildApp')` and interleaves `configBuilder.buildApp(builder)` just before the first `order: 'post'` hook, letting frameworks control environment build order and interdependencies.

`hotUpdate` is the environment-aware replacement for `handleHotUpdate`: `getSortedHotUpdatePlugins(environment)` selects the plugins and each hook receives a `HotUpdateOptions` with `{type, file, timestamp, read, server, modules}` and may return a filtered module list.

Environments are created through configurable factories — `environmentOptions.dev.createEnvironment(name, config, { ws })` at server start and `config.build.createEnvironment(name, config)` in `createBuilder.setupEnvironment` — with `defaultCreateDevEnvironment`/`defaultCreateClientDevEnvironment` as the built-in defaults.

The HMR transport is pluggable on both ends: server-side via `normalizeHotChannel` and `createServerHotChannel()` (exported publicly), client/runtime-side via `normalizeModuleRunnerTransport` and `createWebSocketModuleRunnerTransport` in `src/shared/moduleRunnerTransport.ts`.

`bindCLIShortcuts({ print, customShortcuts })` accepts an array of `CLIShortcut<Server>` objects (`{ key, description, action }`) merged with the built-in table — the mechanism the CLI itself uses to add the `p` profiler toggle.

Plugin hook filtering is an extension point with its own registry: `getCachedFilterForPlugin(plugin, hookName)` builds and WeakMap-caches `createIdFilter` / `createFilterForTransform` matchers from a hook's `filter: { id, code, moduleType }` object.

`createIdResolver(config, options)` is exported as the supported way for plugins to reuse Vite's resolver, and `config.createResolver(options)` wraps it with per-environment `PartialEnvironment` instances for client and ssr.

`create-vite` extends purely by directory convention — each entry in the `FRAMEWORKS` variants table maps to a sibling `template-<name>` directory (`template-react-ts`, `template-svelte`, `template-qwik-ts`, …), so adding a template means adding a directory plus a table entry.

agent_handoff.summary: This is a high-traffic OSS monorepo with strict conventions: pnpm only (enforced by `only-allow` in `preinstall`), oxfmt for formatting, eslint for `packages/*/{src,types}/**/*.ts`, and a `simple-git-hooks` pre-commit running lint-staged. Almost nothing can be verified without first running `pnpm build`, since the playground tests execute the built `dist/node/cli.js`. Read the CLI, server bootstrap, config resolver, and plugin pipeline before touching anything; treat the security guards and the deprecation shims as append-only unless the change is deliberate. The most common trap is editing `packages/vite/src/node` and testing without rebuilding, or adding a runtime dependency to the wrong section of `package.json`.

claims.claim: Read first, in order: `packages/vite/src/node/cli.ts` (command surface), `packages/vite/src/node/server/index.ts` (`_createServer` + middleware order), `packages/vite/src/node/config.ts` (`resolveConfig`, `loadConfigFromFile`), `packages/vite/src/node/plugins/index.ts` (`resolvePlugins` ordering) and `packages/vite/src/node/build.ts` (`createBuilder`/`buildEnvironment`).

Setup is `pnpm i` then `pnpm run build` at the repo root; while developing Vite itself, run `pnpm run dev` inside `packages/vite` for a watching Rolldown rebuild (`premove dist && pnpm build-bundle -w`).
pnpm is mandatory — root `preinstall` runs `npx only-allow pnpm` and `packageManager` pins `pnpm@12.4.2`; npm/yarn installs will be rejected.

Verification commands: `pnpm test-unit` (fast, no browser), `pnpm test-serve [match]` / `pnpm test-build [match]` for targeted playground runs, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` (oxfmt), and `pnpm typecheck` (root `tsc -p scripts` plus every package's own typecheck).

Playground test matching is per-substring and only works on `test-serve`/`test-build`, not on `pnpm test` — e.g. `pnpm run test-serve assets` runs both `playground/assets` and `playground/assets-sanitize`.

Trap: playground tests run against a real `vite` binary resolved through `viteBinPath` in `vitestSetup.ts`, so source edits in `packages/vite/src` are invisible to integration tests until `pnpm build` (or a running `pnpm dev` watcher) regenerates `dist`.

Trap: the e2e global setup copies playgrounds into `playground-temp/` and only copies the directories matched by the selected spec files — a new fixture directory that no spec references will not be copied, and `VITE_PRESERVE_BUILD_ARTIFACTS=1` (via `pnpm debug-build`) is needed to inspect the output.

Dependency placement is a reviewed decision: `packages/vite/package.json` carries a literal `"//": "READ CONTRIBUTING.md to understand what to put under deps vs. devDeps!"` marker, and CONTRIBUTING has sections on `require()` usage, adding dependencies, and ensuring type support.

Formatting and linting are enforced on commit: `simple-git-hooks` pre-commit runs `lint-staged --concurrent false`, which applies `oxfmt` to all files and eslint `--fix` to `packages/*/{src,types}/**/*.ts`, `packages/**/*.d.ts` and `playground/**/__tests__/**/*.ts`.

Safe edit boundary: anything under `playground/` is fixture + spec code, not shipped code — only `packages/vite`, `packages/create-vite` and `packages/plugin-legacy` are published, and CI skips tests entirely for `packages/create-vite/template**` changes.

Do not relax the filesystem guards casually: `isFileLoadingAllowed`, `looksLikeWindowsShortNamePath`, the NTFS-colon check and `rejectInvalidRequestMiddleware` each carry comments identifying a specific bypass class they exist to block.

When adding a server-facing API, mirror the environment convention: put state on `DevEnvironment` (which owns `moduleGraph`, `pluginContainer`, `_pendingRequests`, `transformRequest`, `warmupRequest`, `waitForRequestsIdle`) and expose any flat `server.*` alias only through `warnFutureDeprecation`.
